cards.q: What do the End-to-End Enterprise Scenarios practice?
cards.a: They stitch campus, WAN, data center, security, and automation into one integrated lab, practicing full data-path troubleshooting and the ENCOR big-picture design using a top-down verify chain.

cards.q: What domains are combined in an end-to-end scenario?
cards.a: Campus (L2/L3 + FHRP), WAN (DMVPN/SD-WAN), data center (VXLAN/vPC), security (ACL/firewall), and automation (APIs) — one topology with all domains connected.

cards.q: How do you trace the data path in an end-to-end scenario?
cards.a: Follow one packet end-to-end: host to access, access to distribution, routing to the WAN, tunnel/crypto, then the remote site and server.

cards.q: What is the configuration order for an integrated enterprise lab?
cards.a: Build L2 base, then L3 base, redundancy, WAN/tunnels, security, automation, then verify — building in layers and cross-checking domains.

cards.q: What scenarios are tested in an end-to-end lab?
cards.a: Dual-homed failover, application performance with QoS, cloud extension, security segmentation, and monitoring with telemetry.

cards.q: How is verification performed in a cross-domain lab?
cards.a: Use ping/traceroute for reachability, show commands for state, IP SLA for SLA, NetFlow for flows, and syslog for events — probe, state, flow, then logs across sites.

cards.q: What is the recommended troubleshooting playbook?
cards.a: Establish a baseline, run a failure test, find the root cause, fix it, re-verify, then automate the fix.

cards.q: Which commands are used across branch, campus, and DC in an end-to-end scenario?
cards.a: show ip route, show sdwan control connections, show ip nhrp brief, show crypto session, ping/traceroute across sites, and show switching paths.

cards.q: Cross-site connectivity fails. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A tunnel or crypto issue, so check NHRP and crypto state with show ip nhrp brief and show crypto session.

cards.q: Campus connectivity fails in an end-to-end lab. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A VLAN or FHRP problem, so check the standby state with show standby.

cards.q: Data center traffic fails. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A VXLAN issue, so check the NVE state with show nve peers.

cards.q: The lab is slow or drops traffic unpredictably. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A QoS problem, so check the policy with show policy-map.

cards.q: Traffic is blocked unexpectedly across a segment. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: An ACL or firewall rule, so check the security rules.

cards.q: You should verify each layer independently even in an integrated scenario.
cards.a: True — verify each layer before cross-checking between domains so issues are isolated correctly.

cards.q: When troubleshooting, the most efficient first step is to test from one end to the other without touching intermediate layers.
cards.a: False — follow one packet end-to-end and verify each layer in order before cross-domain checks, which isolates the failing layer.

cards.q: QoS, security, and automation are configured separately and do not interact in an integrated lab.
cards.a: False — QoS, security, and automation are integrated, not silos, in an end-to-end enterprise scenario.

cards.q: What ensures a lab fix actually works and is repeatable?
cards.a: Simulate failures and re-verify after fixes, then encode the fix in a repeatable playbook so it can be automated.

cards.q: How do you validate a full-stack enterprise scenario?
cards.a: Follow one packet end-to-end across all domains, test failover, and check monitoring/telemetry to confirm the full stack works together.
